concept.name: Elastic net
concept.definition: A regularized regression combining the L1 (lasso) and L2 (ridge) penalties, retaining the lasso's variable selection while adding a grouping effect that keeps strongly correlated predictors in or out of the model together. Introduced by Zou and Hastie (2005).
concept.intuition: Pure lasso tends to pick one variable out of a correlated cluster and drop the rest; mixing in ridge penalty makes the whole cluster share the coefficient, which is stabler when predictors travel in packs.
concept.mechanics: beta_hat minimizes (1/2n) ||y - X beta||^2 + lambda [alpha ||beta||_1 + (1-alpha) ||beta||^2 / 2], with alpha mixing lasso (alpha=1) and ridge (alpha=0); both hyperparameters are chosen by cross-validation and the fit is computed by coordinate descent. It is especially useful when p >> n, where lasso saturates at n selected variables.
concept.formula: beta_hat = argmin_b { (1/2n) ||y - Xb||^2 + lambda ( alpha ||b||_1 + (1 - alpha) ||b||^2 / 2 ) }.
concept.failure_modes: Two tuning parameters make selection costlier and more prone to validation overfitting, and as with lasso, naive post-selection inference is invalid.
concept.misconceptions: That elastic net always dominates lasso: with truly sparse, weakly correlated predictors plain lasso is simpler and comparably good; elastic net's advantage concentrates in grouped, collinear designs.
concept.example: Selecting among hundreds of correlated technical indicators, elastic net keeps whole families of similar momentum variants together instead of arbitrarily discarding all but one.
